thesis_statement: Vulcan is the pure-play aggregates compounder: local pricing power (freight-adjusted price +5% mix-adjusted) with cash gross profit per ton above $12 despite energy inflation and disruptive weather, an active acquisition pipeline, and public-construction demand backing the reaffirmed full-year outlook - a high-quality franchise whose volumes still ride the construction cycle.

base.summary: Volumes recover modestly as weather normalizes, pricing holds the 4-5% discipline, and the reaffirmed adjusted EPS outlook delivers with aggregates cash gross profit per ton above $12.
drivers: freight-adjusted price per ton $22.97 +5% mix-adjusted (+4% reported)
public construction activity and large projects supporting shipments

bull.summary: Infrastructure spending accelerates, the acquisition pipeline consolidates local reserves at value-accretive prices, and unit-margin expansion continues compounding the per-ton economics.
drivers: portfolio-enhancing actions completed in Q2 with active M&A pipeline
SAG as % of revenue improving (6.6% vs 6.9%)

bear.summary: Private-construction demand stays weak, weather and energy inflation keep pressuring unit costs (cash cost +7%, or +3% ex-diesel), and the cyclical volumes confirm the de-rating the stock has already taken.
drivers: aggregates shipments only +1% with Texas/Southeast rain impact
~29x trailing for a volume-flat aggregates business

key_risks: Volume stagnation: shipments +1% in Q2 with weather disruption; the per-ton economics are carrying all the growth.
Cost inflation: freight-adjusted unit cash cost +7% (+3% ex-diesel); pricing of +4-5% is only barely outrunning it.
Private residential construction remains the weak leg; public demand is the offset but is budget-dependent.
Valuation: ~29x trailing and ~23x forward is full for a volume-cyclical; the market is pricing per-ton compounding continuing without interruption.
